headline: New Brunswick Parks Entry and Wilderness Lodging
reservation: Daily vehicle permits are required for entry and can be obtained at the park gatehouse. Accommodation at heritage cabins or campgrounds requires separate advance booking through the New Brunswick Parks system. Availability is seasonal, so check the official portal for specific opening and closing dates of facilities.

days.title: The Maritime Peak
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Nictau Gate

stops.name: Mount Carleton Summit
stops.detail: Hike to the highest point in the Maritimes to see the historic fire tower and views reaching toward the Maine border.

stops.name: Mount Head
stops.detail: Traverse the ridge to this neighboring peak for an unobstructed view of the rugged Bathurst Highlands.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes on gravel park roads; conditions vary with weather.
days.note: The summit weather can change rapidly; ensure you have sufficient layers for high-altitude wind.

days.title: Lakeside Heritage and Wildlife

stops.name: Nictau Lake
stops.detail: Launch a canoe to view Mount Bailey reflecting in the water, a prime spot for spotting resident loons.

stops.name: Williams Falls
stops.detail: Follow a short, accessible trail to these picturesque falls tucked within the old-growth forest.

days.driving: Minimal; local transfers between lakeside trailheads.
days.note: Moose are frequently sighted near the lake margins at dawn and dusk; drive with caution.

days.title: The Volcanic Peaks of the North
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the park office

stops.name: Mount Sagamook
stops.detail: Take the steep ascent for a vertical challenge and a panoramic view of the entire park's lake system.

stops.name: Pine Point
stops.detail: Stroll along the shores of Bathurst Lake through rare red pine stands found in this specific microclimate.

days.driving: Allow 20–30 minutes; watch for logging trucks on access roads.
days.note: Sagamook is one of the park's most strenuous hikes; allow ample time for the descent.

intel.title: The Last Fuel Stop
intel.text: Fill your tank in Saint-Quentin or Bathurst before heading toward the park. There is no fuel available within the park or on the immediate approach roads.

intel.title: Digital Dead Zone
intel.text: Expect zero cellular reception throughout the park. The park office has a public phone for emergencies, but satellite devices are recommended for remote hiking.

intel.title: Gravel Road Navigation
intel.text: Most internal roads are well-maintained gravel but can be dusty or muddy depending on rainfall. Lower-clearance vehicles should proceed slowly to avoid tire damage.

intel.title: Daylight Awareness
intel.text: The park is heavily forested and shadows fall early in the deep valleys. Plan to be off the summit trails well before sunset to navigate the rocky terrain safely.

intel.title: Trailhead Logistics
intel.text: Parking at the Mount Carleton trailhead is limited; arriving before 10 AM is suggested during summer months. Overflow parking may require walking along the roadway.

plan.arrival: Fly into Bathurst (ZBF), rent a vehicle, and purchase all grocery supplies in town, as the park interior is purely wilderness.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are preferred for gravel roads, though standard cars are permitted; check for spare tire equipment.
plan.goldenHour: Pine Point on Bathurst Lake offers a stunning view of the sunset light hitting the eastern slopes of Mount Sagamook.
